clinical_notes:
We are seeing this 57-year-old woman today for a follow-up visit, and the history today is as follows. Several toenails are thick, yellow and crumbly. The sleep evaluation found loud snoring, pauses in breathing seen by the bed partner and daytime sleepiness, with an Epworth score of 19. The sleep evaluation found loud snoring, pauses in breathing seen by the bed partner and daytime sleepiness, with an Epworth score of 17. The pt came to the visit alone.

PMH:
Hyperlipidemia, on a statin. Followed by primary care since 2016.
Hypothyroidism, stable on replacement.
Family history is noncontributory.
Laser surgery for nearsightedness in 2010.
Carpal tunnel release in 2016.
Tonsillectomy as a child.
Shoulder tendon repair in 2006.
Father with an underactive thyroid.
Mother with osteoporosis.
A brother w/ migraines.
Inguinal hernia repair in 2021.

Current medications:
levothyroxine 75 mcg daily
metformin 500 mg twice daily, no side effects reported

ALLERGIES/INTOLERANCES:
Codeine (nausea).

Social history:
Works as an accountant. Former smoker, quit years ago. No alcohol.

Examination:
Blood pressure 125/73, pulse 74, temperature 98.6 F, oxygen saturation 96% on room air. Well-appearing and in no distress. Loud snoring, witnessed pauses in breathing, a body mass index of 39 and a crowded airway make moderate to severe sleep apnea very likely. Skin is warm & dry. Neck: supple, no lymphadenopathy, no thyromegaly. HEENT: normocephalic, atraumatic; oral mucosa moist. Abdomen: soft, nontender, nondistended, nl bowel sounds. Skin: warm & dry, no rash on exposed areas.

Results:
The diagnostic study last month showed moderate sleep apnea, and a CPAP titration study is needed. Most recent blood counts were unremarkable. Lipid panel on 06/23/2026: LDL 89 mg/dL on the current statin dose. Thyroid-stimulating hormone 2.8 on 09/11/2026, within the reference range. Basic metabolic panel on 07/20/2026: sodium 136, potassium 4.1, creatinine 0.9. Blood couunt on 09/18/2026: white count 5.2, hemoglobin 13.8, platelets 259.

Assessment:
1. Obstructive sleep apnea (adult) (pediatric) (G47.33)
2. Tinea unguium (B35.1)
3. Hyperlipidemia, unspecified (E78.5)
4. Hypothyroidism, unspecified (E03.9)

Disposition:
Procedure planned: overnight lab sleep study with CPAP titration, pt 6 or older. A copy of this note goes to the primary care physician. Return precautions were reviewed. The patient was given written information about the visit, including how to reach the clinic after hours & when to call. Today's findings and the next steps were explained in plain language, & the patient repeated the plan back accurately. Metformin 500 mg twice daily was renewed for 90 days. The patient's preferred contact method was updated. Next routine visit is planned in about 3 wks. Time was spent reviewing the medication list with the pt, confirming doses & the pharmacy on file. Outside records from the prior clinic were scanned into the chart.
